title: Never-before-Seen Titanic Artifact Just Landed in Denver - NewsBreak
text: Be the first to see a letter sent directly from the Titanic at the Molly Brown House Museum! This, and many more never-before-seen artifacts, are the centerpieces of the museum’s latest exhibit, See Justice Done: The Legacy of the Titanic Survivors’ Committee . The exhibit is open and runs through September 21, 2025. For the first time ever, a Titanic letter written by survivor Archibald Gracie will be on public display. Gracie wrote to a friend while on board the ill-fated ship using Titanic’s own stationery. His letter included a foreboding message: “It is a fine ship but I shall await my journey’s end before I pass judgment on her.” Museum Director, Andrea Malcomb, has shared that, “The Molly Brown House Museum is deeply honored to have been chosen to be the first museum to exhibit such an important Titanic artifact. This letter supports two additional letters written by Col. Archibald Gracie just weeks before his death that are held in the museum’s collection. Gracie had been corresponding with Margaret Brown about her Titanic experience to include in his forthcoming book, The Truth About Titanic .” Other rare artifacts include a letter written by Margaret to her daughter Helen days after the Titanic disaster, filling in details of her experience, a mysterious flag with a patch that reads, “From the crew survivors to Mrs. J. J. Brown,” and the Egyptian talisman that survived the Titanic sinking in Mrs. Brown’s pocket. Visit the museum to see these and other fascinating artifacts linked to Margaret’s Titanic experience! See Justice Done is included in general Molly Brown House Museum admission. Upcoming Titanic events include: Margaret's Birthday Tea Soiree Help us celebrate Margaret Brown's birthday in style and raise some money for the museum at the same time! Experience a rare opportunity to mingle with Brown family descendants who are just as witty and accomplished as their foremother! Great-granddaughter Helen is a speaker, fundraiser, and Doberman Mom, and great-granddaughter Lynne is retired in Santa Fe with her three cats and enjoys gardening, studying the Upanishads, and grappling with Sanskrit. Meet these amazing women, explore rare Titanic artifacts, and enjoy birthday cake, tea goodies, and sip on a special birthday cocktail or mocktail. It'll be the "Bee's Knees!” Friday, July 18 at 5:30 p.m. The Wreck of the Titan, or Futility – The Official Autograph Facsimile Edition™ Book Launch Event Before the Titanic set sail, a book described its fate. Over a century later, that book is returning to print—and it’s launching in the home city of Titanic’s most iconic survivor. The Wreck of the Titan, or Futility , a 1912 novella by Morgan Robertson eerily foreshadowed the sinking of the Titanic. Presented by Denver-based Open Kimono Publishing, this marks the first official re-release of The Wreck of the Titan, or Futility in over 100 years. The event will feature a live talk with the author of the edition’s foreword, and signed, limited copies will be available. Thursday, July 17 at 6:30 PM. Author Discussion with Steven Schwankert- The Six: The Untold Story of the Titanic's Chinese Survivors Join us in the historic home of Titanic Survivor, Margaret "Molly" Brown, as we welcome author Steven Schwankert to discuss and sign copies of his recently released book and documentary project "The Six: The Untold Story of the Titanic's Chinese Survivors," where he will share how six Chinese men survived the Titanic against all odds. The result of meticulous research, a dogged investigation, and interviews with family members, The Six is an epic journey across continents that reveals the full story of these six forgotten survivors. The Titanic continues to reveal a multitude of secrets, and the lives of these six men add a layer of humanity and nuance to one of the most storied shipwrecks in history. Saturday, August 30 at 3:00 p.m. Aug 7, 28, Sept 18 – Titanic Exhibit Deeper Dive Tour – Join us for an in-depth tour in the home of Titanic survivor, Margaret "Molly" Brown as we explore new Titanic artifacts in the See Justice Done exhibit that tells the experience of Margaret Brown who was declared the heroine of the Titanic by newspapers for her ability to comfort and raise money for Titanic’s immigrant passengers, and stand up for the surviving crew. If museum collections are your passion too, consider supporting our Curator Stephanie McGuire and her work to care for and add to our collections. Donate today, specifying “MB Curator” with your gift! And become a member of Historic Denver today, to help us tell all the stories that make Denver, Denver! #
